targets.authors: Beilock, S. L., Gunderson, E. A., Ramirez, G., & Levine, S. C.
targets.title: Female teachers' math anxiety affects girls' math achievement.
targets.evidence_quote: In the current study, we sought to replicate and extend the results of Beilock et al. (2010) with a larger sample.
targets.outcome_quote: Replicating their overall finding, we too found that when elementary school teachers were anxious about math, their students learned less math across the school-year. Importantly, unlike the previous work that showed the influence of teachers' math anxiety was limited to female students, in this higher-powered study, we found a negative relation between teachers' math anxiety and children's math achievement for both boys and girls, consistent with recent research on other caregivers' math anxiety (i.e., mothers' math anxiety) and children's math learning in elementary school (Maloney et al., 2015; Schaeffer et al., 2018).
targets.outcome_reasoning: The central negative association agrees, but the authors explicitly contrast the gender-specific finding. Confirmation of the overall finding is an effect-specific statement, not an overall replication verdict that overrides the stated contrast. Additional stereotype non-replication was visible but is not needed for this verdict.
